beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:setting it up, knowingly]^Everyone knows the story: the greatest library of the ancient world, in ^Alexandria, in Egypt, ^burned to the ground.

[d:calm][p:0.93][act:setting the scene, easy]Alexandria: a great ^port on Egypt's Mediterranean coast. [act:placing it in time]Egypt's ^Greek kings founded the library there around {285|two eighty-five} BCE, some twenty-three ^centuries ago. [act:amused, a modern touch]Less a reading room, more a ^research institute, with scholars on ^salaries.

[d:aside][p:0.93][act:explaining, light]Its books were ^scrolls of papyrus, a paper made from ^reeds. [act:lightly, holding up the number]^Ancient writers claim up to ^seven hundred thousand scrolls. [act:dry, a small smile]^Modern historians ^doubt it: numbers like that tend to grow in the ^telling.

[d:build][p:0.93][act:detective, relishing it]So who ^did it? [act:setting up the line-up]^Four suspects. [act:the line-up, one by one][tune:level]Julius ^Caesar, the Roman general, at war in the city in {48|forty-eight} BCE. [act:next suspect, same pace][tune:level]The Roman emperor ^Aurelian, {272|two seventy-two} CE. [act:keeping the rhythm][tune:level]The city's ^bishop, in {391|three ninety-one}. [act:the last one, landing it][tune:fall]And a ^caliph, ruler of the Arab empire, in {642|six forty-two}.

[d:build][p:0.93][act:the method, detective]Historians test each one like a detective checking an ^alibi: if the victim is seen ^alive after the attack, that attack wasn't ^fatal. [act:laying out evidence]After Caesar's fire, the Greek geographer ^Strabo worked at the institute. [act:dry, the alibi holds]It was ^still running.

[d:build][act:careful, precise]In {391|three ninety-one}, a ^temple was destroyed, the Serapeum. [act:even, weighing the sources]Writers of the time describe a temple falling, but ^none says it ^still held a great library.

[d:reveal][sfx:hit][act:the reveal, slower]And the caliph story? [p:0.93][act:explaining, even]It first appears about five hundred and ^sixty years after the Arab conquest. [p:0.9][act:the everyday picture, clear]Like a first report, written ^today, of something from the ^fourteen-sixties. [p:0.93][act:calm, scholarly]Historians call it a late ^invention.

[d:build][go:5|0][p:0.93][act:thoughtful, counting them off]What killed the library was ^slower: royal ^funding ran out, scholars were expelled in {145|one forty-five} BCE, wars wrecked the palace quarter. [p:0.9][act:the key idea, quiet]And papyrus doesn't last ^forever: books nobody ^recopied by hand simply crumbled ^away.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm][tune:rise]^One great fire? [act:the verdict, firm][tune:fall]*Ruled ^out*. [act:turning it over][tune:rise]A great ^loss of knowledge? [act:sincere, simple][tune:fall]^Real. [act:quiet, the key idea][tune:fall]And ^slow.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:gentle, thoughtful][tune:fallrise]Libraries don't ^only burn. [gap:0.45][act:the last word, quiet][tune:fall]They ^starve.
